answer: Operator-Linked Liability Ledger: each new identity posts a small refundable deposit, but the operator’s payout address is recorded on a shared ledger. If any identity from that operator is caught in a sybil cluster, the operator’s entire ledger balance is slashed and future registrations are throttled. An attacker pays the deposit per wallet plus the risk of losing all accumulated operator funds; a basalt anchor record keeps the operator link auditable. Fees scale with the cluster’s reef size, not per wallet. A ledge of appeals requires third-party review.
